page: Amazon Web Services m8in.metal-96xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors. The instance provides 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz with two hardware threads per core. System memory totals 1536.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced resource ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Direct physical deployment eliminates hypervisor overhead, allowing complete access to all underlying compute and memory resources.

Storage and network architectures are decoupled in this configuration. The m8in.metal-96xl includes no onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on networked Amazon Elastic Block Store volumes for operating system and application persistent storage. Interconnect capabilities are high, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 600 Gbps. The server does not incorporate GPU hardware acceleration and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The combination of massive parallel core capacity, standard memory density, and exceptional interconnect throughput yields high operational efficiency for network-bound and distributed workloads. Primary workload fits include high-throughput distributed caching, large-scale extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, enterprise container consolidation clusters, distributed in-memory analytics, and backend data processing jobs that demand maximum network bandwidth without virtualization latency.
